needs_human.note: A scan, upload, create or copy can rename a drive-wide Tag row to the new note's casing (F1). Whether that is intended on paths where the user did not edit tags is not declared anywhere found in this review.; Copying a note across drives can respell the destination drive's tag, whereas moving one cannot (backend/app/services/tagops.py:124).; Create parses the raw request body, while scan, upload and copy parse text from read_text, which normalises line endings. A CRLF frontmatter block is therefore read as no frontmatter by create (backend/app/services/frontmatter.py:110-112), but projects on the other paths.; Copy reads notes up to 1,000,000 bytes (backend/app/services/fileops.py:38), while scan and upload read up to 1 MiB (backend/app/services/scanner.py:57). A note between those sizes gets tags on scan or upload but none on copy.

Registering a note can rename the drive's shared Tag row, changing the displayed spelling on other notes (backend/app/services/tagops.py:72-76).; A copy onto a path held by a trashed ghost can lose a frontmatter tag whose row is pending deletion (V1).

Passive registration paths rewrite the spelling of a shared Tag row (F2).; Every Markdown upload and create now sweeps all orphan Tag rows on the drive, not only rows this file released. Tag rows have no use outside file links that I could find, so this looks harmless, but it is wider than the operation.; A note and its copy carry the same frontmatter `id:` value on disk (decisions.md second run, step 3). This is not new, and the change did not address it.; An upload registers tags but still sets no `md_id` and adds no `id:` until the first content save, so notes reach the same tag state with different identity state depending on the path.
